Drug Development Leaders Share RAS Findings at Global Symposium
 FORT MYERS, Fla. , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Studies of emerging approaches to targeting RAS mutations, including two first-in-human clinical trials, conducted with participation from Florida Cancer Specialists & Research Institute, LLC (FCS) are being presented at the 38 th EORTC-NCI-AACR (ENA) Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics this week in Barcelona, Spain.
 RAS (Rat sarcoma) genes help regulate cell growth, division and signaling. Mutations in these genes, particularly KRAS, NRAS and HRAS, contribute to the development of several common and historically difficult-to-treat cancers, including colorectal, lung and pancreatic cancers.
 "Targeting RAS mutations is a major priority in advancing the next generation of cancer therapies," said Manish R. Patel, MD , who directs activities at the statewide practice's two drug development units in Sarasota and Central Florida dedicated exclusively to Phase 1 clinical trials in partnership with Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI). Dr. Patel is co-author of the following abstract being presented at ENA 2026:
 A First-in-Human Phase 1/2 Study of SAR449336, an Oral Non-Covalent Pan-KRAS Inhibitor, in Patients With Advanced KRAS-Mutant Solid Tumors (Trial in Progress) (338) 
 Associate Director of Drug Development Judy Wang, MD , who oversees clinical trials offered at the FCS Sarasota Drug Development Unit and serves as principal investigator on a multitude of early-phase trials, will deliver the following oral presentations:
 Preliminary safety, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy of ERAS-0015: Results from the AURORAS-1 first-in human trial (8) 
 Preliminary clinical results of QTX3034, an oral G12D-preferring KRAS inhibitor, in patients with KRASG12D-mutated endometrial cancer (9LBA) 
 "I am honored to present our research alongside global leaders in drug development and contribute to the scientific exchange that is advancing our understanding of cancer biology, emerging therapeutic targets and new treatment approaches," Dr. Wang said.
 Additionally, Dr. Wang and Cesar Perez, MD , director of the Drug Development Unit at the Sarah Cannon Research Institute at FCS in Lake Nona , contributed to the following abstract being presented at ENA 2026:
 Preliminary phase 1 results from AVENTINE-1, a phase 1/2 study of ACZO-1418, an EGFR-HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate (BsADC) for the treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors (81) 
 "Our continued commitment to clinical research reinforces the important role community oncology plays in advancing cancer care and bringing access to new therapies closer to where patients live," added Dr. Wang.
 Through partnerships with SCRI—one of the world's leading oncology research organizations conducting community-based clinical trials—and Paradigm Health, Inc., FCS offers convenient access to clinical trials at nearly 30 locations statewide, including its drug development units.
 All accepted abstracts will be published online at ENA2026 .
 About Florida Cancer Specialists & Research Institute, LLC: (FLCancer.com)
 For more than 40 years, Florida Cancer Specialists & Research Institute (FCS) has embraced innovation to deliver world-class care and drive the dramatic transformation of oncology care through its robust clinical research program.
 FCS provides patients with access to a wide range of clinical trials, positioning it as a leader in research among private oncology practices in Florida and across the country. Through its robust clinical research program with Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI) and a suite of independent site management programs, with advanced clinical trial matching technology, FCS offers patients innovative therapies close to home. Each year, FCS conducts more than 180 active clinical trials that directly elevate patient care and accelerate progress in oncology. Many of the cancer drugs approved by the FDA in the U.S over the past decade were accessible to patients at FCS through clinical trial participation before receiving approval.
 Our outstanding team of highly trained and dedicated physicians is committed to delivering tailored treatment plans that make the best use of cutting-edge precision oncology advancements to enhance patient outcomes.

Die Zulassung durch die Europäische Kommission folgt auf die kürzlich erteilte Zulassung von Biocons Pertuzumab-Biosimilar durch die US-amerikanische FDA 
 Biocons Pertuzumab bietet eine zusätzliche Behandlungsoption für Patientinnen mit HER2-positivem Brustkrebs und kann zu nachhaltigeren Gesundheitssystemen in Europa beitragen 
 Dieser Meilenstein stärkt das wachsende Onkologie-Portfolio von Biocon und das Engagement des Unternehmens, den sich wandelnden Bedürfnissen von Patientinnen sowie den Anforderungen im Gesundheitswesen gerecht zu werden 
 BENGALURU, Indien , 18. November 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Biocon Limited (BSE: 532523) (NSE: BIOCON), ein weltweit tätiges innovatives biopharmazeutisches Unternehmen, gab heute bekannt, dass die Europäische Kommission (EK) die Marktzulassung für Pebrilzo®, Biocons Pertuzumab-Biosimilar, zur Behandlung von HER2-positivem Brustkrebs in verschiedenen Krankheitsstadien in der Europäischen Union (EU) erteilt hat.
 Das Pertuzumab-Biosimilar von Biocon ist das erste Biosimilar, das im Rahmen des neuen fokussierten klinischen Ansatzes der Europäischen Arzneimittelagentur (EMA) eine EU-Zulassung erhalten hat. Dieser Meilenstein folgt auf die positive Stellungnahme des Humanarzneimittelausschusses (CHMP) der Europäischen Arzneimittelagentur (EMA) vom 17. September 2026. 1 
 Shreehas Tambe, CEO und Geschäftsführer von Biocon, sagte: „Die Zulassung unseres Pertuzumab-Biosimilars Pebrilzo® durch die Europäische Kommission als erstes Biosimilar im Rahmen des neuen, fokussierten klinischen Ansatzes ist ein weiterer wichtiger regulatorischer Meilenstein für Biocon. Mit dieser Zulassung wird Pertuzumab zu unserem fünften onkologischen Biosimilar, das sowohl in Europa als auch in den Vereinigten Staaten zugelassen ist. Dies stärkt unser globales Onkologie-Portfolio und bekräftigt unser Engagement, Patienten mit HER2-positivem Brustkrebs einen besseren Zugang zu hochwertigen und erschwinglichen biologischen Therapien zu ermöglichen." 
 Informationen zum Wirkstoff:
 Biocons Pertuzumab-Biosimilar, das als 420-mg-Konzentrat zur Herstellung einer Infusionslösung zugelassen ist, ist ein Biosimilar-Arzneimittel. Der Wirkstoff ist Pertuzumab, ein monoklonaler Antikörper, der mit hoher Affinität und Spezifität an den humanen epidermalen Wachstumsfaktorrezeptor 2 (HER2) bindet und so die Vermehrung von Tumorzellen hemmt, die HER2 überexprimieren.
 Das Pertuzumab-Biosimilar von Biocon ist zur Anwendung in Kombination mit Trastuzumab und einer Chemotherapie bei der neoadjuvanten Behandlung von erwachsenen Patientinnen mit HER2-positivem, lokal fortgeschrittenem oder entzündlichem Brustkrebs oder mit HER2-positivem Brustkrebs im Frühstadium mit hohem Rezidivrisiko sowie zur adjuvanten Behandlung von erwachsenen Patientinnen mit HER2-positivem Brustkrebs im Frühstadium mit hohem Rezidivrisiko indiziert.
 Darüber hinaus ist es zur Anwendung in Kombination mit Trastuzumab und Docetaxel bei erwachsenen Patientinnen mit HER2-positivem metastasiertem oder lokal rezidivierendem, inoperablem Brustkrebs indiziert, die zuvor noch keine Anti-HER2-Therapie oder Chemotherapie gegen ihre metastasierte Erkrankung erhalten haben.
 Umfassende, orthogonale und dem neuesten Stand der Technik entsprechende strukturelle und funktionelle analytische Charakterisierungen sowie vergleichende klinische pharmakokinetische Daten haben gezeigt, dass Biocons Pertuzumab-Biosimilar dem Referenzprodukt in hohem Maße ähnlich ist und keine klinisch bedeutsamen Unterschiede hinsichtlich Qualität, Sicherheit oder Wirksamkeit aufweist.
 Biocon in der Onkologie
 Biocon baut sein Engagement in der Onkologie weiter aus. Das Portfolio umfasst unter anderem Therapien gegen solide Tumoren wie Brustkrebs sowie unterstützende Behandlungen bei chemotherapiebedingter Neutropenie. Zum Portfolio gehören auch Therapien gegen Osteoporose, behandlungsbedingten Knochenverlust und Skelettkomplikationen im Zusammenhang mit fortgeschrittenen Krebserkrankungen 2 . Das Pertuzumab-Biosimilar stärkt das Portfolio des Unternehmens und erweitert die Möglichkeiten, Patienten in verschiedenen Phasen ihrer Krebsbehandlung zu unterstützen.
 Epidemiologie: 
Brustkrebs ist nach wie vor die am häufigsten diagnostizierte Krebserkrankung bei Frauen in Europa. Nach Schätzungen des Europäischen Krebsinformationssystems (ECIS) aus dem Jahr 2024 ist Brustkrebs die häufigste Krebsdiagnose bei Frauen in ganz Europa 3 . Etwa 15–20 % der invasiven Brustkrebserkrankungen sind durch eine HER2-Überexpression oder -Amplifikation gekennzeichnet 4 . Trotz bedeutender Fortschritte bei der HER2-gerichteten Therapie unterstreicht die Belastung durch Brustkrebs die Bedeutung eines breiten und nachhaltigen Zugangs zu hochwertigen Behandlungsoptionen in den europäischen Gesundheitssystemen. 2,3 
 Über Biocon Limited
 Biocon Limited (BSE: 532523, NSE: BIOCON) ist ein weltweit tätiges biopharmazeutisches Unternehmen, dessen Ziel es ist, Patienten weltweit erschwingliche, lebensverbessernde Medikamente zur Verfügung zu stellen. Mit Hauptsitz in Bengaluru, Indien, widmet sich Biocon einigen der drängendsten Herausforderungen im Gesundheitswesen im Bereich chronischer und nicht übertragbarer Krankheiten, indem es sowohl Biosimilars als auch Generika in großem Maßstab in verschiedenen Regionen anbietet. Mit diesem breit gefächerten Portfolio konzentriert sich Biocon auf Bereiche mit hohem ungedecktem Bedarf, die wichtige Therapiebereiche wie Diabetes, Onkologie, Adipositas, Herz-Kreislauf-Erkrankungen, Immunologie, Augenheilkunde und Knochengesundheit umfassen. Das Unternehmen hat mehrere Branchenneuheiten eingeführt, die die globale Biosimilar-Landschaft mitgeprägt haben. Bis heute hat das Unternehmen weltweit 12 Biosimilar-Produkte und mehr als 30 Generika auf den Markt gebracht. Es verfügt über eine solide Forschungs- und Entwicklungspipeline mit mehr als 20 Biosimilar-Projekten sowie GLP-1-Peptiden und anderen komplexen Generika. Mit einem integrierten „Lab-to-Patient"-Modell vereint Biocon Forschung und Entwicklung, Produktion und Vermarktung, um eine zuverlässige und skalierbare Versorgung mit Medikamenten sicherzustellen. Das Unternehmen ist in mehr als 120 Ländern tätig und wird dabei von sieben Produktionsstandorten, drei F&E-Standorten, 18 Niederlassungen weltweit und einer Belegschaft von über 9.500 Mitarbeitern unterstützt. Biocon wurde zum vierten Mal in Folge in das S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook 2026 aufgenommen, was sein Engagement für nachhaltiges und verantwortungsbewusstes Wachstum unterstreicht. text:
La autorización de la CE se produce tras la reciente aprobación del pertuzumab de Biocon por parte de la FDA estadounidense. 
 Ofrece una opción terapéutica adicional para pacientes con cáncer de mama HER2 positivo y puede contribuir a unos sistemas sanitarios más sostenibles en Europa. 
 Este hito refuerza la creciente cartera de Biocon en oncología y su compromiso con la evolución de las necesidades de los pacientes y los sistemas sanitarios. 
 BENGALURU, India , 18 de noviembre de 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Biocon Limited (BSE: 532523; NSE: BIOCON), compañía biofarmacéutica global centrada en la innovación, ha anunciado hoy que la Comisión Europea (CE) ha concedido la autorización de comercialización a Pebrilzo®, su biosimilar de pertuzumab, para el tratamiento del cáncer de mama HER2 positivo en distintas fases de la enfermedad en la Unión Europea (UE).
 El biosimilar de pertuzumab de Biocon es el primero en recibir la autorización de comercialización de la CE mediante el nuevo enfoque clínico adaptado de la Agencia Europea de Medicamentos (EMA). Este hito se produce tras el dictamen favorable emitido por el CHMP el 17 de septiembre de 2026. 1 
 Shreehas Tambe, CEO y director general de Biocon , ha declarado: « La aprobación por parte de la Comisión Europea de Pebrilzo®, nuestro biosimilar de pertuzumab, el primero autorizado en el marco de su nueva vía clínica adaptada, representa un importante hito regulatorio para Biocon. Con esta aprobación, pertuzumab se convierte en nuestro quinto biosimilar oncológico aprobado tanto en Europa como en Estados Unidos, reforzando nuestra cartera global de oncología y nuestro compromiso de ampliar el acceso a terapias biológicas de alta calidad y asequibles para pacientes con cáncer de mama HER2 positivo.». 
 Información sobre el medicamento:
 El biosimilar de pertuzumab de Biocon, aprobado como concentrado de 420 mg para solución para perfusión, es un medicamento biosimilar cuyo principio activo es pertuzumab, un anticuerpo monoclonal que se une con gran afinidad y especificidad al receptor 2 del factor de crecimiento epidérmico humano (HER2), inhibiendo la proliferación de las células tumorales que sobreexpresan HER2.
 El biosimilar de pertuzumab de Biocon está indicado, en combinación con trastuzumab y quimioterapia, para el tratamiento neoadyuvante de pacientes adultos con cáncer de mama HER2 positivo localmente avanzado, inflamatorio o en estadio temprano con alto riesgo de recurrencia. También está indicado para el tratamiento adyuvante de pacientes adultos con cáncer de mama HER2 positivo en estadio temprano y alto riesgo de recurrencia.
 Asimismo, está indicado en combinación con trastuzumab y docetaxel para pacientes adultos con cáncer de mama HER2 positivo metastásico o localmente recurrente no resecable que no hayan recibido previamente tratamiento anti-HER2 ni quimioterapia para la enfermedad metastásica.
Una exhaustiva caracterización analítica estructural y funcional mediante técnicas ortogonales de última generación, junto con datos comparativos de farmacocinética clínica, demostró que el biosimilar de pertuzumab de Biocon presenta un alto grado de similitud con el medicamento de referencia, sin diferencias clínicamente relevantes en términos de calidad, seguridad o eficacia.
 Biocon en oncología
 Biocon mantiene un compromiso sólido y creciente con la oncología y cuenta con una cartera que abarca distintos ámbitos de la atención oncológica, incluidos los tumores sólidos, como el cáncer de mama, así como tratamientos de soporte para abordar la neutropenia inducida por la quimioterapia. Este compromiso se extiende también a la salud ósea, con tratamientos dirigidos a la osteoporosis, la pérdida ósea asociada a los tratamientos y las complicaciones esqueléticas vinculadas a cánceres avanzados 2 . El biosimilar de pertuzumab amplía aún más la oferta de la compañía y refuerza su capacidad para apoyar a los pacientes a lo largo de las distintas etapas de la atención oncológica y en diferentes sistemas sanitarios.
 Epidemiología:
 El cáncer de mama continúa siendo el cáncer diagnosticado con mayor frecuencia entre las mujeres en Europa. Según las estimaciones de 2024 del Sistema Europeo de Información sobre el Cáncer (ECIS), es el tipo de cáncer más diagnosticado entre las mujeres en Europa. Aproximadamente entre el 15 % y el 20 % de los cánceres de mama invasivos presentan sobreexpresión o amplificación de HER2. Additional funding brings total funding commitment to $9.79 million and supports GMP manufacturing and IND-enabling toxicology for a Phase 1 clinical study 
 WALTHAM, Mass. , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Akagera Medicines, Inc., a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing lipid nanoparticle (LNP) therapeutics and vaccines for infectious diseases that disproportionately affect the majority of low- and middle-income countries, today announced that the Gates Foundation has expanded its grant supporting the company's dendritic cell-targeted LNP mRNA vaccine for the prevention of tuberculosis (TB). The new award adds $7,806,414 in funding, bringing the total committed under the grant to $9,791,826.
 The grant, titled " Dendritic cell targeted lipid nanoparticle mRNA vaccines to prevent TB " (Investment ID INV-058409), continues a preclinical feasibility and development program first funded in 2023. The expanded funding will support GMP manufacturing of clinical trial material and the IND-enabling toxicology studies ahead of a future regulatory filing and before a first-in-human (FIH) Phase 1 clinical trial.
 TB remains the world's deadliest infectious disease, causing more than one million deaths each year. BCG, the only licensed TB vaccine, is more than a century old and offers limited and variable protection against pulmonary TB in adolescents and adults, the populations that drive most transmission. A safe, effective vaccine for these groups is widely regarded as essential to ending the TB epidemic.
 Akagera's vaccine candidate pairs mRNA-encoded Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens with an LNP engineered to preferentially deliver its payload to dendritic cells, the immune system's most potent antigen-presenting cells. By directing antigen expression to these cells, the approach is designed to drive the strong, durable T-cell responses believed to be central to protection against TB, while potentially enabling lower doses and improved tolerability.
 Under the initial 2023 award, Akagera established preclinical feasibility of the dendritic cell-targeted platform. The preclinical findings showed robust immunogenicity in animal models using an mRNA vaccine candidate coding for nine unique tuberculosis antigens and demonstrating recognition of the TB antigens in human peripheral blood immune cells in vitro. The expanded grant moves the program from discovery into development, funding:
 Process development and GMP manufacturing of the mRNA-LNP drug product for clinical use
 IND-enabling GLP toxicology and safety pharmacology studies
 Preparation of the regulatory package to support a future IND (or equivalent) filing and a first-in-human Phase 1 trial
 "This expanded support from the Gates Foundation marks the transition of our TB vaccine program from proof of concept to clinical readiness," said Daryl Drummond, Ph.D., Co-Founder and Chief Scientific Officer of Akagera Medicines. "Targeting mRNA delivery to dendritic cells lets us focus on the immune response where it matters most for TB. With manufacturing and IND-enabling toxicology now funded, we have a clear path to our first-in-human study."
 "Tuberculosis falls hardest on the communities with the least access to new medicines," said Michael Fairbanks, Co-Founder and Executive Chairman of Akagera Medicines. "The Gates Foundation's continued funding lets us advance a vaccine designed from the start for the people and places that need it most, alongside our long-acting TB therapeutic, AKG-100."

 Akagera Medicines, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing lipid nanoparticle formulations of antibacterial drugs and mRNA vaccines for tuberculosis and other infectious diseases, including RSV, influenza, Lassa fever and HIV. First-in-human dosing of DTI-117, an investigational on-demand therapy being developed for neurogenic bowel dysfunction 
 NIH-funded, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study is evaluating single intramuscular doses in healthy volunteers 
 Preliminary topline data expected in early 2027 
 RESEARCH TRIANGLE PARK, N.C., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dignify Therapeutics ("Dignify", the "Company"), a biopharmaceutical development company focused on restoring bowel and bladder control for people with neurological conditions, today announced that the first participant was dosed on November 17 in its Phase 1 study of DTI-117, an investigational on-demand treatment being developed for people with neurogenic bowel dysfunction (NBD).
 The study ( NCT07882472 ) is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of single ascending intramuscular doses of DTI-117 in healthy volunteers. It is designed to assess safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics and is funded by the National Institutes of Health (NIH). The study is expected to enroll up to 40 participants across up to five sequential dose cohorts. Within each cohort, participants are randomized to receive DTI-117 or placebo. Preliminary topline data from the initial cohorts are anticipated in early 2027.
 People with NBD can have difficulty evacuating on their own, which can make bowel care time consuming and dependent on caregiver assistance. Existing approaches such as laxatives, enemas and manual evacuation can be unpredictable in timing, invasive or stigmatizing.
 "For people with neurogenic bowel dysfunction, bowel care often takes significant time and effort and depends on a caregiver. DTI-117 is designed to return control of timing to the person who needs it," said Karl Thor, Ph.D., Chief Scientific Officer of Dignify Therapeutics. "Dosing the first participant begins establishing, in people, the safety and exposure profile on which any future benefit for patients will depend."
 "Dignify was founded on the belief that people with neurological conditions should be able to decide when they empty their bowel and bladder, rather than plan their lives around the condition," said Anthony DiTonno, Chief Executive Officer of Dignify Therapeutics. "With the first participant dosed, DTI-117 is now being evaluated in people, and we look forward to sharing preliminary topline data in early 2027."
 About DTI-117
 DTI-117 is a novel, short-acting peptide and neurokinin-2 receptor agonist being developed by Dignify Therapeutics as an on-demand treatment for neurogenic bowel dysfunction and other bladder and bowel voiding disorders. DTI-117 is designed to produce rapid, transient emptying with a short duration of action suited to patient-controlled voiding. With the IND clearance, DTI-117 is currently being evaluated in a NIH-funded randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 single-ascending-dose study evaluating DTI-117 in healthy participants.
 About Dignify Therapeutics
 Founded by a team of serial entrepreneurs and internationally recognized scientists, Dignify Therapeutics' mission is to provide practical and convenient treatments for bladder and bowel voiding dysfunction, especially in people with neurogenic conditions. The Company has been supported by founders, venture capital firms, the North Carolina Biotechnology Center, the One NC Small Business Program, and the NIH. Dignify has received 18 NIH awards and more than $20 million in NIH funding. Dignify Therapeutics is located at the First Flight Venture Center in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina. DTI-117 development is supported by the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke of the NIH under Award Number U44NS129628. Largest analysis of LEQEMBI LEADER study reported to date includes findings on amyloid clearance in routine clinical practice, delayed progression to moderate or severe AD, expanded subcutaneous maintenance experience, and additional sex-based outcomes 
 TOKYO and CAMBRIDGE, Mass. , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eisai Co., Ltd. and Biogen Inc. (Nasdaq: BIIB ) today announced new three-year real-world findings of 560 patients across 13 U.S. clinical sites from the largest analysis of the ongoing Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease (LEADER) study* reported to date. New LEADER findings from a pre-specified analysis show a 76% lower rate of progression to moderate or severe Alzheimer's disease dementia with LEQEMBI ® compared to a matched natural history cohort. The data were presented alongside an additional international real-world meta-analysis of approximately 5,000 patients at the 19th Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease (CTAD) Conference in Boston.
 "As Alzheimer's disease progresses, patients and families can experience increasing challenges that affect cognition and function," said Brent Berry, M.D., Ph.D., Minneapolis Clinic of Neurology. "The LEADER study is helping us understand how the benefits of continued LEQEMBI treatment seen in the Clarity AD clinical trial carry over into routine clinical practice. These real-world findings from sites across the U.S. suggest that continued treatment with LEQEMBI may help keep patients in the early stages of Alzheimer's disease for longer. They also add to our understanding of treatment persistence, subcutaneous maintenance therapy and safety across diverse clinical settings, which can help inform treatment decisions with patients and families."
 Key Findings from the LEADER Study 
 LEADER Patients Showed Slower Progression Compared to ADNI Control** 
 In a pre-specified comparison of LEADER (N=504) and an ADNI-weighted external control cohort (N=573) through 36 months, LEQEMBI patients in the study had a 76% lower rate of progression to moderate or severe AD dementia (HR 0.24; 95% CI, 0.15-0.39).
 More Than 8 in 10 Patients Remained Stable or Improved* ** 
 Among the 546 people with early AD whose change in disease stage could be assessed after an average of approximately 18 months of treatment, 81.1% of patients were reported as stable (75.8%) or improved (5.3%) compared with baseline.
 Results were generally consistent across groups defined by sex, race, ethnicity, APOE genotype and concomitant antithrombotic-use groups.
 Among all 560 patients, 87.5% remained on LEQEMBI treatment at the time of chart extraction, with an average treatment duration of approximately 19 months.
 Most Patients Estimated to Remain in Early AD Through Three Years 
 Among all 560 patients receiving LEQEMBI in the overall study, 95.0% were estimated to remain in the early stages of AD through three years (36 months) of treatment, based on statistical modeling of observed real-world patient data.
 New Real-World Evidence Shows Complete Amyloid Clearance 
 At sites performing both baseline and follow up amyloid PET data, 77% of patients (N=33 of 43 across 6 sites) became amyloid-negative at a median follow up of 18.1 months (IQR 16.4–18.7 months).
 Expanding Experience with LEQEMBI Maintenance Therapy 
 Of the patients who reached 18 months of treatment, 91.7% remained on LEQEMBI treatment. A total of 218 patients transitioned to once-every-four-weeks intravenous (IV) maintenance therapy and, following its subsequent approval, 64 patients transitioned to once-weekly subcutaneous (SC) maintenance therapy.
 71.1% of patients on monthly IV maintenance treatment and 76.6% on weekly SC maintenance treatment remained stable after an average of 26 months and 25.1 months following treatment initiation, respectively.
 All 64 patients receiving SC maintenance therapy remained on therapy at the time of chart extraction.
 No ARIA**** events were reported during the subcutaneous maintenance period and there were no other safety events of significance. There was a 0.5% incidence of isolated ARIA-H reported during the IV maintenance period.
 Clinical Outcomes Consistent Between Women and Men 
 79.3% of women (N=300) and 83.3% of men (N=246) in the study were reported as stable or improved.***
 Treatment duration and persistence were similar across sexes, with 86.0% of females and 88.9% of males remaining on therapy at time of chart extraction. 
 ARIA incidence and severity were generally consistent between female and male patients: any ARIA (14.7% females vs. 17.0% males), ARIA-E (7.5% females vs. 5.5% males), ARIA-H (9.8% females vs. 12.6% males), isolated ARIA-H (7.2% females vs. 11.5% males).
 LEADER Safety Findings Consistent with ALZ-NET Real-World Experience
 Overall safety findings in LEADER were consistent with the independent ALZ-NET registry and U.S. prescribing information for LEQEMBI.
 ALZ-NET is a North American voluntary health care provider-enrolled patient network that collects longitudinal clinical, imaging, and safety data in patients treated with FDA-approved AD therapies. Over 1,700 patients taking LEQEMBI were included in ALZ-NET at the time of data extraction.
 ARIA-E was observed in 6.6% of patients in LEADER, compared with 6.3% in ALZ-NET, while ARIA-H was observed in 11.1% of patients in LEADER, compared with 10.1% of patients in ALZ-NET.
 Observed ARIA rates were generally consistent regardless of APOE ε4 status, concomitant antithrombotic use, race and ethnicity.
 Additional International Real-World Meta-Analysis Evaluates Approximately 5,000 Patients *****
 A separate post hoc-exploratory analysis presented at CTAD evaluated 16 published real-world LEQEMBI cohorts across six countries, representing approximately 5,000 patients treated in routine clinical practice.
 Key findings include:
 Rates of ARIA were lower than those reported in Clarity AD. Across the 16 real-world studies, the pooled average total ARIA rate was 12.4% compared to 21.5% in Clarity AD, ARIA-E rate was 4.0% compared to 12.6% in Clarity AD, and the ARIA-H rate was 9.4% compared to 17.3% in Clarity AD.
 Symptomatic ARIA was 0.8% compared to 2.8% in Clarity AD.
 Treatment discontinuation due to adverse events was 3.2%.
 *The three-year LEADER Study is a multicenter, retrospective real-world study designed to examine LEQEMBI utilization, treatment persistence, transition to maintenance therapy, safety, cognitive and functional assessments, and healthcare professional (HCP) implementation learnings in diverse U.S. clinical settings for patients with early AD. The study integrated deidentified chart and electronic medical record (EMR) data from 13 U.S. sites, HCP surveys and HCP interviews. This updated analysis included 560 patients with early AD who, as of September 2026, received at least seven LEQEMBI initiation infusions. The maintenance therapy analysis included patients who received biweekly IV initiation treatment for 18 months, followed by at least three months of IV or SC maintenance therapy.
 **ADNI is a clinical research project launched in 2005 to develop methods to predict the onset and progression of AD and to confirm the effectiveness of treatments. The project involves a multi-year longitudinal observation targeting healthy elderly individuals as well as patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and early stages of AD.
 ***Change in clinical disease stage was defined as:
 Stable: Patient remaining in the same clinical disease stage (MCI due to AD or mild AD dementia) from baseline throughout the course of LEQEMBI treatment.
 Improvement: Patient transitioning from mild AD dementia at baseline to MCI due to AD over the course of LEQEMBI treatment.
 Progression: Patient advancing from MCI at baseline to mild/moderate AD dementia or from mild AD dementia at baseline to moderate AD dementia throughout the course of LEQEMBI treatment.
 ****ARIA refers to amyloid-related imaging abnormalities that can be observed with anti-amyloid beta antibody treatment and includes ARIA-E, which involves edema/effusion, and ARIA-H, which involves hemosiderin deposition, including cerebral microhemorrhage, cerebral macrohemorrhage and superficial siderosis, as observed on brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
 *****The meta-analysis on ARIA rates and safety profiles in clinical practice included centers located in the U.S., China, South Korea, Japan, Italy and Israel. Patients were treated between 2023 and 2026 and received at least six months of LEQEMBI treatment.

 About lecanemab (generic name, brand name: LEQEMBI ® )
 Lecanemab is the result of a strategic research alliance between Eisai and BioArctic. It is a humanized immunoglobulin gamma (IgG1) monoclonal antibody directed against aggregated soluble (protofibril) and insoluble forms of amyloid-beta (Aβ).
Lecanemab has been approved in 53 countries and regions including Japan, the United States, China, Europe, South Korea, Taiwan, and Saudi Arabia, and is under regulatory review in 6 countries. Following the initial phase with treatment every two weeks for 18 months, intravenous (IV) maintenance dosing with treatment every four weeks was approved in 9 countries including the U.S., China, the UK, and others, and applications have been filed in 11 countries and regions. The U.S. FDA approved Eisai's Biologics License Application (BLA) for subcutaneous maintenance dosing (360mg) with LEQEMBI IQLIK in August 2025. For subcutaneous initiation treatment (500 mg), approval was obtained in the U.S. in July 2026 and China and Japan in September 2026, and applications are under review in 4 countries.
Since July 2020 the Phase 3 clinical study (AHEAD 3-45) for individuals with preclinical AD, meaning they are clinically normal and have intermediate or elevated levels of amyloid in their brains, is ongoing. AHEAD 3-45 is conducted as a public-private partnership between the Alzheimer's Clinical Trial Consortium that provides the infrastructure for academic clinical trials in AD and related dementias in the U.S., funded by the National Institute on Aging, part of the National Institutes of Health, Eisai and Biogen. Since January 2022, the Tau NexGen clinical study for Dominantly Inherited AD (DIAD), that is conducted by Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network Trials Unit (DIAN-TU), led by Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, is ongoing and includes lecanemab as the backbone anti-amyloid therapy.
 About Protofibrils
 Protofibrils are believed to contribute to the brain injury that occurs with AD and are considered to be the most toxic form of soluble Aβ, having a primary role in the cognitive decline associated with this progressive, debilitating condition. 1 Protofibrils cause injury to neurons in the brain, which in turn, can negatively impact cognitive function via multiple mechanisms, not only increasing the development of insoluble Aβ plaques but also increasing direct damage to brain cell membranes and the connections that transmit signals between nerve cells or nerve cells and other cells. It is believed the reduction of protofibrils may prevent the progression of AD by reducing damage to neurons in the brain and cognitive dysfunction. 2
 Limitations of Real-World Studies
 Retrospective real-world studies can be valuable in providing additional information to complement clinical trial data; however, there are potential limitations to consider, including: potential for biases, data completeness and consistency, lack of a control group, interpretation of data due to lack of placebo-controlled arms, and confounding variables, and data inconsistency. Data inconsistency may be mitigated by providing site access to standardized electronic case-report forms.

Longer-term results from the Phase 2 CELIA study suggest clinical benefit may build over time 
 NEW YORK , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today at the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease (CTAD) conference in Boston, Biogen presented new data from the Phase 2 CELIA study of diranersen (BIIB080), an investigational therapy designed to reduce the production of tau in people with early Alzheimer's disease. The new data, which suggest diranersen's clinical benefit may grow with longer treatment, build on results presented in July, when the drug produced strong reductions in tau and signals of slowed cognitive decline, despite missing its primary endpoint.
 "CELIA gave the field its first evidence from a randomized trial that lowering tau may slow cognitive decline, and today's two-year data suggest that benefit may build over time," said Laura Nisenbaum, PhD, Interim Chief Science Officer of the ADDF. "The lowest dose appeared to perform best, but its safety and clinical benefit will need to be confirmed in a larger Phase 3 trial. Importantly, diranersen also lowered tau without affecting amyloid, making it a promising candidate to pair with anti-amyloid therapies as the field works toward combination treatments that address the full pathobiology of Alzheimer's."
 The late-breaking symposium featured 96-week efficacy and safety data from the study's ongoing long-term extension. Among participants on the lowest dose, Biogen reported a 38% slowing of decline at two years on CDR-SB, a measure of cognition and daily function, up from 26% at 18 months. Biogen said that dose offered the best balance of benefit and side effects, and no new safety signals were reported.
 While progress on tau, one of the two defining pathologies of Alzheimer's, is an important step for the field, effectively treating this disease will require novel therapies that target its complete pathobiology. Today's pipeline shows we are well on our way: of the 158 drugs now in clinical trials, nearly 75% are aimed at biology beyond amyloid and tau. Through its venture philanthropy model, the ADDF has helped fuel that diversity, backing novel targets and the biomarkers needed to treat the disease from multiple angles.
 "Every new dataset on tau moves us closer to treating Alzheimer's the way we already treat cancer, with combinations of therapies tailored to each patient," said Isobel Coleman, Chief Executive Officer of the ADDF. "Trials like this one show what becomes possible when the field invests in targets beyond amyloid. The ADDF will continue to back the full range of approaches the field needs to make precision medicine a reality for people living with Alzheimer's."
 About The Alzheimer's Drug Discovery Foundation (ADDF)
 Founded in 1998 by Leonard A. and Ronald S. Lauder, the Alzheimer's Drug Discovery Foundation is dedicated to rapidly accelerating the development of drugs to prevent, treat, and cure Alzheimer's disease. The ADDF is the only public charity solely focused on funding the development of drugs for Alzheimer's, employing a venture philanthropy model to support research in academia and the biotech industry. The ADDF's leadership and contributions to the field have played a pivotal role in bringing the first Alzheimer's PET scan (Amyvid®) and blood test (PrecivityAD®) to market, as well as fueling the current robust and diverse drug pipeline. Through the generosity of its donors, the ADDF has awarded nearly $400 million to fund 792 Alzheimer's drug development, biomarker, and prevention programs in 21 countries. L'autorisation de la Commission européenne fait suite à la récente approbation du pertuzumab de Biocon par la FDA américaine. 
 Offre une option thérapeutique supplémentaire aux patients atteints d'un cancer du sein HER2 positif et pourrait contribuer à des systèmes de santé plus durables en Europe. 
 Cette nouvelle étape vient renforcer le portefeuille de Biocon en oncologie, en pleine expansion, et confirme son engagement à répondre à l'évolution des besoins des patients et des systèmes de santé 
 BENGALURU, Inde , 18 novembre 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Biocon Limited (BSE : 532523 ; NSE : BIOCON), entreprise biopharmaceutique multinationale axée sur l'innovation, annonce aujourd'hui que la Commission européenne a accordé une autorisation de mise sur le marché à Pebrilzo®, son biosimilaire du pertuzumab, pour le traitement du cancer du sein HER2 positif à différents stades de la maladie dans l'Union européenne (UE).
 Le biosimilaire du pertuzumab de Biocon est le premier biosimilaire à obtenir une autorisation de mise sur le marché de la Commission européenne dans le cadre de la nouvelle approche clinique de l'Agence européenne des médicaments (EMA) 1 . Cette autorisation fait suite à l'avis favorable rendu le 17 septembre 2026 par le Comité des médicaments à usage humain (CHMP).
 Shreehas Tambe, directeur général et Managing Director de Biocon , a déclaré : « L'autorisation de Pebrilzo® par la Commission européenne, notre biosimilaire du pertuzumab et le premier à être approuvé dans le cadre de sa nouvelle approche clinique adaptée, marque une étape réglementaire majeure pour Biocon. Avec cette autorisation, le pertuzumab devient notre cinquième biosimilaire en oncologie approuvé à la fois en Europe et aux États-Unis, renforçant ainsi notre portefeuille mondial en oncologie et réaffirmant notre engagement à élargir l'accès des patients atteints d'un cancer du sein HER2 positif à des traitements biologiques de haute qualité et accessibles. » 
 Informations sur la molécule :
 Le biosimilaire du pertuzumab de Biocon, autorisé sous forme de solution à diluer pour perfusion dosée à 420 mg, est un médicament biosimilaire dont la substance active est le pertuzumab, un anticorps monoclonal ciblant, avec une forte affinité et une grande spécificité, le récepteur 2 du facteur de croissance épidermique humain (HER2). Il inhibe ainsi la prolifération des cellules tumorales surexprimant HER2.
 Le biosimilaire du pertuzumab de Biocon est indiqué, en association avec le trastuzumab et une chimiothérapie, dans le traitement néoadjuvant des patients adultes atteints d'un cancer du sein HER2 positif localement avancé, inflammatoire ou précoce présentant un risque élevé de récidive. Il est également indiqué dans le traitement adjuvant des patients adultes atteints d'un cancer du sein précoce HER2 positif présentant un risque élevé de récidive.
 Il est par ailleurs indiqué, en association avec le trastuzumab et le docétaxel, chez les patients adultes atteints d'un cancer du sein HER2 positif métastatique ou localement récidivant non résécable, n'ayant pas reçu auparavant de traitement anti-HER2 ni de chimiothérapie pour leur maladie métastatique.
Une caractérisation analytique approfondie, structurale et fonctionnelle, reposant sur des méthodes complémentaires de pointe et complétée par des données comparatives de pharmacocinétique clinique, a démontré que le biosimilaire du pertuzumab de Biocon est hautement similaire au médicament biologique de référence, sans différence cliniquement pertinente en matière de qualité, de sécurité ou d'efficacité.
 Biocon en oncologie
 Biocon renforce son engagement de longue date en oncologie, avec un portefeuille couvrant plusieurs domaines de la prise en charge du cancer : les tumeurs solides, notamment le cancer du sein, mais aussi les soins de support, avec des traitements de la neutropénie chimio-induite. Cet engagement s'étend à la santé osseuse, avec des traitements de l'ostéoporose, de la perte osseuse liée aux traitements et des complications osseuses des cancers avancés 2 . Le biosimilaire du pertuzumab enrichit ce portefeuille et renforce la capacité de l'entreprise à accompagner les patients à chaque étape de leur parcours de soins en cancérologie, au sein de systèmes de santé variés.
 Épidémiologie :
 Le cancer du sein reste le cancer le plus fréquemment diagnostiqué chez les femmes en Europe, selon les estimations de 2024 du Système européen d'information sur le cancer (ECIS). Environ 15 à 20 % des cancers du sein invasifs se caractérisent par une surexpression ou une amplification de HER2. Malgré les progrès considérables des traitements ciblant HER2, le poids du cancer du sein souligne l'importance de garantir un accès large et pérenne à des traitements de qualité dans l'ensemble des systèmes de santé européens. 3,4 
 À propos de Biocon Limited 
 Biocon Limited (BSE : 532523, NSE : BIOCON) est une entreprise biopharmaceutique mondiale dont la mission est de fournir aux patients du monde entier des médicaments abordables qui contribuent à améliorer leur vie. Basée à Bengaluru, en Inde, Biocon répond à certains des défis de santé les plus pressants à l'échelle mondiale dans les maladies chroniques et non transmissibles grâce à une offre de biosimilaires et de médicaments génériques commercialisés à grande échelle sur différents marchés. Biocon concentre ses activités sur des domaines thérapeutiques où les besoins médicaux restent importants, notamment le diabète, l'oncologie, l'obésité, les maladies cardiovasculaires, l'immunologie, l'ophtalmologie et la santé osseuse. L'entreprise a également contribué à faire progresser le secteur des biosimilaires à travers plusieurs innovations pionnières. À ce jour, Biocon a commercialisé 12 biosimilaires et plus de 30 médicaments génériques dans le monde. Son portefeuille de recherche comprend plus de 20 programmes de biosimilaires, ainsi que des peptides GLP-1 et d'autres médicaments génériques complexes en développement. Grâce à un modèle intégré couvrant l'ensemble de la chaîne de valeur, de la recherche au patient, Biocon réunit des capacités de recherche et développement, de production et de commercialisation afin de garantir un approvisionnement fiable et durable en médicaments. L'entreprise est présente dans plus de 120 pays, s'appuie sur sept sites de production, trois centres de R&D et 18 bureaux dans le monde, et emploie plus de 9 500 collaborateurs. Early adopter program aims to scale Ten63 ' s BEYOND platform across challenging pharmaceutical targets 
 DURHAM, N.C. , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ten63 Therapeutics, Inc. ("Ten63") today announced the launch of BEYOND-Alpha, an early adopter program through which select pharmaceutical companies will work with Ten63 to apply its BEYOND computational drug design platform. Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. ("Chugai") is the first pharmaceutical company to participate in the BEYOND-Alpha program.
 Through BEYOND-Alpha, a limited number of early participants will work with Ten63 to apply BEYOND across challenging targets. BEYOND-Alpha is designed to allow Ten63's computational design infrastructure to operate across multiple drug discovery programs in parallel.
 " AI changes the economics of drug discovery because computational molecular design can scale in a way conventional experimental discovery cannot, " said Marcel Frenkel, Ph.D., Co-Founder and CEO of Ten63 Therapeutics. " Scale isn ' t the only advantage. BEYOND is designed to tackle targets historically considered undruggable or intractable. " 
 As part of BEYOND-Alpha, Ten63 will apply its proprietary computational drug design platform, BEYOND, to Chugai-nominated targets that present challenges for conventional small-molecule discovery approaches. Ten63 will generate and rank molecular structures designed against each target. Chugai will have the right to negotiate terms for the further research, development, and commercialization of molecules including the structures generated by Ten63 against each target, subject to the execution of a separate definitive agreement.
 " Chugai is one of the most innovative drug discovery organizations in the world, with an exceptional track record of pursuing new science and challenging therapeutic targets. That makes them an ideal first participant in BEYOND-Alpha, " added Frenkel. 
 Chugai's participation in BEYOND-Alpha expands on the investment from Chugai Venture Fund, the corporate venture arm of Chugai, in Ten63 ' s strategic financing announced in February 2026 . 
 About BEYOND 
 BEYOND is Ten63's computational drug design platform for generative chemistry, built to maintain accuracy across low-data and challenging targets. In recent prospective studies across diverse protein targets, BEYOND-generated designs achieved SPR-confirmed hit rates ranging from 11-75%, including against targets for which leading co-folding methods had previously produced few or no confirmed binders. Across these programs, hit identification was achieved by synthesizing and assaying fewer than 20 molecules per program. BEYOND combines high-fidelity physics-based simulation with AI, enabling Ten63 to search in excess of 100 trillion synthetically accessible molecules and design candidates against protein targets long regarded as intractable, including targets lacking conventional binding pockets.
 About the BEYOND-Alpha Program 
 BEYOND-Alpha is Ten63's early adopter drug design program, created to demonstrate the scalability of Ten63's BEYOND platform across pharmaceutical discovery portfolios. It provides a limited number of pharmaceutical participants with the opportunity to apply BEYOND across challenging drug targets. Ten63 applies its computational design technology to generate and prioritize molecular structures against participant-nominated targets, enabling participants to evaluate multiple potential molecular starting points before determining whether to pursue broader development and licensing relationships.

 Ten63 is a frontier AI drug-discovery company spun out of Duke University and TTIC and headquartered in the Research Triangle, North Carolina. Phase 2 clinical trial published in Cell Reports Medicine finds JAK inhibitor safely reduces immune overactivity, improves inflammatory skin conditions and opens new avenues for research on brain health and Alzheimer's disease 
 The takeaway: Researchers at the Linda Crnic Institute for Down Syndrome at the University of Colorado Anschutz found that tofacitinib, a medication that targets an overactive immune signaling pathway, reduced inflammation and improved certain inflammatory skin conditions in adolescents and adults with Down syndrome. The phase 2 clinical trial, published in Cell Reports Medicine, also identified preliminary improvements on selected neurobehavioral assessments, although larger, placebo-controlled studies are needed to determine whether the medication improves neurological function.
 AURORA, Colo. , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In a first-of-its-kind clinical trial, researchers at the Linda Crnic Institute for Down Syndrome (Crnic Institute) at the University of Colorado Anschutz found that a medication targeting immune overactivity in people with Down syndrome reduced underlying inflammation and was associated with improvements in inflammatory skin conditions, while opening new avenues for research on brain health and Alzheimer's disease.
 Patients at the Linda Crnic Institute for Down Syndrome 
 Patients at the Linda Crnic Institute for Down Syndrome 
 The phase 2 clinical trial of tofacitinib, a medication known as a JAK inhibitor that blocks certain signals involved in immune responses and inflammation, was published today in Cell Reports Medicine .
 The findings provide important evidence that targeting underlying immune dysregulation may offer a new approach to addressing multiple health conditions associated with Down syndrome.
 Why researchers targeted immune hyperactivity in Down syndrome 
 Down syndrome is caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21, which carries genes encoding several receptors for interferons, molecules that regulate immune responses. Previous research by the Crnic Institute established that this genetic change contributes to chronically elevated interferon signaling and widespread immune dysregulation. The new study tested whether reducing this excessive signaling could be a viable therapeutic approach.
 How the phase 2 clinical trial for JAK inhibition worked 
 The research team enrolled adolescents and adults with Down syndrome who also had inflammatory skin conditions, such as hidradenitis suppurativa and alopecia areata. Participants received tofacitinib twice daily for 16 weeks, with an optional extension to 40 weeks. The trial included extensive safety monitoring, dermatological evaluations, blood-based molecular analyses and neuropsychological assessments. The study also evaluated changes in biological markers associated with brain health and Alzheimer's disease.
 "This study represents an important milestone in our efforts to develop new treatments for people with Down syndrome," said Joaquín Espinosa, PhD, executive director of the Crnic Institute, professor of pharmacology, and senior author of the study. "We have demonstrated that we can reduce excessive immune activity and improve certain inflammatory conditions. The results of this study lay the groundwork for future clinical trials that could address a broader range of conditions associated with Down syndrome."
 Study finds reduced inflammation and improvements in skin conditions 
 The study met its predefined safety endpoint, with a safety profile similar to that observed in the general population. The findings do not eliminate the known risks of JAK inhibitors and larger studies will be needed to assess long-term safety in Down syndrome.
 Blood analyses showed significant reductions in interferon activity, inflammatory cytokine scores and metabolites associated with inflammation, including quinolinic acid, a compound with known neurotoxic effects. Extensive analyses of gene expression, circulating proteins, and metabolites showed that tofacitinib modified specific inflammatory pathways rather than completely shutting down immune responses.
 "One of the most exciting findings is that we could bring several abnormal inflammatory markers closer to the levels observed in people without Down syndrome," said Angela Rachubinski, PhD, first author of the study. "Importantly, this medication appears to calm an overactive immune system without weakening normal immune defenses in people with Down syndrome, which may explain its encouraging safety profile."
 Participants also showed improvements in inflammatory skin conditions, particularly hidradenitis suppurativa, which causes painful skin lesions, and alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition that causes hair loss. Improvements were documented through standardized clinical scores and measures of dermatology-related quality of life.
 Neurobehavioral findings are promising but preliminary 
 The investigators additionally observed improved performance on selected tests of attention, memory, vocabulary and behaviors, along with favorable changes in some participant- and caregiver-reported measures of well-being. These findings are preliminary: because the study had no placebo comparison group, researchers cannot determine whether the observed changes were caused by tofacitinib rather than practice effects or other factors.
 "The neuropsychological results are intriguing, but they are not yet proof that this medicine improves cognition," said Lina Patel, PsyD, a study coauthor and professor of psychiatry at CU Anschutz. "What this study establishes is an opportunity to ask more precise questions about which improvements may be due to treatment, while continuing to prioritize participant safety."
 These findings may help advance research into how chronic immune overactivity affects the brain and whether targeting inflammation could improve brain health in people with Down syndrome. Researchers documented favorable changes in several biomarkers related to neurological function and Alzheimer's disease, opening new avenues of future research.
 Based on the results from this first trial, researchers launched a second trial focused on Down Syndrome Regression Disorder, a condition characterized by sudden loss of neurological function that has been associated with inflammatory processes affecting the brain. Results from this second trial are expected to be available in 2027.
 The research builds on the Crnic Institute's Human Trisome Project , which has mapped immune and molecular changes associated with Down syndrome. By comparing trial findings with those earlier datasets, the team identified biological changes that may be responsive to JAK inhibition and biomarkers for monitoring treatment effects.
 "As the mother of my amazing 23-year-old daughter Sophia, it is deeply moving to see the Crnic Institute's groundbreaking research, which GLOBAL supported from the beginning, lead to promising clinical results," said Michelle Sie Whitten, president and CEO of the Global Down Syndrome Foundation. "We are grateful to the NIH INCLUDE Project and to Dr. Joaquín Espinosa and his team for focusing on scientific discoveries leading to longer, healthier lives."
 What the findings mean for future Down syndrome treatments 
 The authors emphasize that tofacitinib is not approved specifically for Down syndrome and that the study does not establish a general treatment recommendation. The findings support further randomized, placebo-controlled studies to evaluate clinical benefits, optimal participant selection and longer-term safety.
 The study, "A phase 2, open-label, single-arm clinical trial of the safety and efficacy of the JAK1/3 inhibitor tofacitinib in Down syndrome," is registered as NCT04246372 ( https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04246372 ). Funding included the NIH INCLUDE Project, the Global Down Syndrome Foundation, the Anna and John J. Sie Foundation and the Ruth E. Olleman Trust.
 Key Points 
 Researchers at the Linda Crnic Institute for Down Syndrome at the University of Colorado Anschutz tested tofacitinib, a JAK inhibitor, in adolescents and adults with Down syndrome.
 The phase 2 clinical trial found reductions in overactive interferon signaling and other markers of inflammation.
 Participants experienced improvements in certain inflammatory skin conditions, including hidradenitis suppurativa and alopecia areata.
 Exploratory neurobehavioral assessments showed encouraging changes, but the study cannot establish that tofacitinib caused these improvements.
 Tofacitinib is not approved specifically for Down syndrome. Larger, randomized clinical trials are needed to evaluate effectiveness and long-term safety.
 About the Linda Crnic Institute for Down Syndrome 
 The Linda Crnic Institute for Down Syndrome is one of the only academic research centers fully devoted to improving the lives of people with Down syndrome through advanced biomedical research spanning from basic science to translational and clinical investigations. Founded through the generous support and partnership of the Global Down Syndrome Foundation , the Anna and John J. Sie Foundation , and the University of Colorado , the Crnic Institute supports a thriving Down syndrome research program involving over 50 research teams across four campuses on the Colorado Front Range. To learn more, visit www.crnicinstitute.org or follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X, Bluesky and LinkedIn @CrnicInstitute. 
 About the University of Colorado Anschutz 
 The University of Colorado Anschutz is a world-class academic medical campus leading transformative advances in science, medicine, education and patient care. The campus includes the University of Colorado's health professional schools, more than 60 centers and institutes, and two nationally ranked independent hospitals - UCHealth University of Colorado Hospital and Children's Hospital Colorado - which see more than 3 million adult and pediatric patient visits each year. Innovative, interconnected and highly collaborative, CU Anschutz delivers life-changing treatments, exceptional patient care and top-tier professional training. The campus conducts world-renowned research supported by over $1 billion in funding, including more than $860 million in sponsored awards and nearly $180 million in philanthropic gifts for research.

 The Global Down Syndrome Foundation (GLOBAL) is the largest nonprofit in the U.S. working to save lives and dramatically improve health outcomes for people with Down syndrome. GLOBAL established the first Down syndrome research institute and supports over 400 scientists and over 2,700 patients with Down syndrome from 40 states and 11 countries. Working closely with Congress and the National Institutes of Health, GLOBAL is the lead advocacy organization in the U.S. for Down syndrome research and care. For Immediate Release: 
 November 18, 2026 
 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Infilbray (venglustat) tablets, the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher disease (GD3) in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kg (approximately 33 pounds). Infilbray crosses the blood-brain barrier to reduce the accumulation of harmful substances in the body and brain.
 “For patients with Type 3 Gaucher disease, harmful substances build up in the brain without a way to stop them, but this drug's ability to cross the blood-brain barrier means it can get to the source of the buildup driving the neurological symptoms,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D.  “This approval reflects the FDA’s commitment to advancing therapeutic options for patients with rare diseases and brings an important new treatment to patients and the healthcare providers who care for them.”
 GD3 is a rare, inherited condition in which the body cannot properly break down fatty substances, called glucosphingolipids, due to a deficient or malfunctioning enzyme. As these substances accumulate in organs, tissues, and the brain, patients experience a wide range of serious health problems over time. Unlike type 1 Gaucher disease, GD3 also affects the brain and nervous system, causing difficulties with balance, coordination, speech, memory, and thinking — symptoms that can worsen progressively and significantly impact quality of life. Infilbray works as a glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor, reducing the buildup of harmful substances throughout the body and, critically, within the brain.
 The FDA’s approval of Infilbray is supported by data from a randomized, double-blind, multicenter clinical study enrolling 43 patients aged 12 years and older with GD3 who had previously been treated with enzyme replacement therapy and had achieved systemic disease stabilization. Participants received either Infilbray orally once daily or intravenous enzyme replacement therapy every two weeks for 52 weeks. Treatment effectiveness was evaluated using two assessments that capture the neurological symptoms central to daily life in patients with GD3, including those related to ataxia (loss of muscle control and coordination) and cognitive function. At Week 52, patients treated with Infilbray demonstrated improvement on a measure that combined both assessments compared to those taking enzyme replacement therapy for the treatment of non-neurologic manifestations of GD3.
 The most frequently reported side effects of Infilbray include gastrointestinal symptoms as well as adverse effects on mood. Serious psychiatric risks, including suicidal ideation and behavior, have been reported. Potential risks identified from animal studies include potential clouding of vision in younger patients and adverse effects on fetal development when drug is taken during pregnancy. More information on side effects can be found in the drug labeling.

In the news release, Cytonics Uses Ten Years of Osteoarthritis Natural-History Data to Shape the Next Stage of CYT-108 Clinical Development, issued 18-Nov-2026 by Cytonics Corporation over PR Newswire, we are advised by the company that changes have been made. The complete, corrected release follows, with additional details at the end:
 Cytonics Uses Ten Years of Osteoarthritis Natural-History Data to Shape the Next Stage of CYT-108 Clinical Development
 FOCAL analysis of the NIH-sponsored Osteoarthritis Initiative identifies two reproducible structural phenotypes of knee osteoarthritis, including a subgroup that loses joint space about 56% faster 
 Findings are informing patient selection and endpoint strategy for the planned Phase 1b/2a study of CYT-108 ahead of Cytonics' planned FDA Type C meeting request 
 JUPITER, Fla. , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cytonics Corporation, a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing engineered alpha-2-macroglobulin (A2M) biologics, today announced the completion of the core analysis of FOCAL (Foundational Osteoarthritis Clinical & Analytic Layer). FOCAL is the company's data-science program for studying how knee osteoarthritis progresses and for turning that knowledge into clinical-trial design decisions for CYT-108, its investigational engineered A2M biologic.
 Continue Reading
 CYT-108 - Cytonics’ investigational therapy being developed for osteoarthritis 
 FOCAL used ten years of follow-up data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI), a multi-center, longitudinal, observational study of knee osteoarthritis sponsored by the National Institutes of Health. Using data from the 4,796-participant OAI cohort, Cytonics selected an analytical population of 1,862 participants with Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grade 2–3 knee osteoarthritis and no prior knee replacement, according to prespecified criteria. It modeled their structural decline on X-ray and MRI, along with their progression to total knee replacement.
 Key findings 
 Two reproducible structural phenotypes. An unsupervised machine-learning analysis (consensus clustering) divided trial-eligible participants into two groups. About four in ten were Severe-Structural and the rest were Early-Structural . The groups were defined in one half of the cohort and reproduced in the other half, with 98.2% label stability.
 Faster progression in the Severe-Structural group. Over ten years, Severe-Structural participants lost joint space about 56% faster per three-year interval than Early-Structural participants (p<0.001, adjusted for baseline joint space, age, sex, BMI and KL grade). They were about three times as likely to undergo total knee replacement within ten years (16.7% vs. 5.5%).
 Confirmation by two imaging methods. The faster decline appeared both in radiographic joint-space width and in quantitative MRI measurement of cartilage thickness. These are independent measurement methods.
 A candidate trial population. Within the Severe-Structural group, applying a minimum joint-space width of 2.0 mm excludes knees too advanced to show further measurable change. The resulting population held up in held-out data, and about one in six OAI participants with usable baseline X-rays met the criteria. Few participants in this population progressed to knee replacement within three years (2.1%), so dropout from that cause would be limited over a typical study period.
 Bone marrow lesions as an added signal. Bone marrow lesions seen on MRI independently predicted faster structural progression. This finding comes from a smaller subset of participants with MRI scoring data and is considered preliminary.
 All FOCAL findings describe the natural course of disease in untreated OAI participants. They do not show or imply any effect of CYT-108. 
 How FOCAL is guiding clinical development 
 FOCAL was set up to answer one question before more patients are enrolled: what would it take to detect a meaningful treatment effect in knee osteoarthritis? 
 The answers are already changing Cytonics' clinical development plans in three ways. 
 Who to enroll. The phenotype and joint-space criteria give Cytonics a candidate way to enrich the planned Phase 1b/2a study for patients whose disease is active and still measurable.
 What to measure, and when. The data show how slowly structure changes, even in faster-progressing patients. The analysis indicates that a trial designed to show a structural benefit would likely need about three years of follow-up and roughly 175 to 300 patients. Based on these results, Cytonics' clinical team concluded that structural measures are not appropriate primary endpoints for an early-stage study. The planned Phase 1b/2a study is being designed to evaluate safety and pain along an escalating dose range. Joint-space width and MRI cartilage measures will be assessed as exploratory endpoints. Disease modification remains the long-term development goal for CYT-108, and FOCAL now gives the company a quantitative basis for designing the longer trials that goal will require.
 How to reduce noise. Bone marrow lesions predict structural progression, but they are also associated with knee pain. Cytonics is therefore evaluating whether to stratify or restrict enrollment by lesion status to protect the reliability of pain measurements. The FOCAL team is also reviewing the pain data available in the OAI to inform recruitment criteria and approaches to limiting placebo response, which is a recurring challenge in osteoarthritis trials. 
 "Osteoarthritis trials have a long history of falling short. Often that happens because the disease moves too slowly, or too unevenly, for a study to see a treatment effect. The drug itself may never get a fair test," said Joey Bose, President and Chief Executive Officer of Cytonics. "Before asking more patients to take part in a study of CYT-108, we wanted to understand the disease we are trying to change. Ten years of untreated natural history told us who progresses, how fast, and how long it takes to see structural change. We are modifying our clinical approach to match that evidence. FOCAL is now a working tool for important design decisions ahead of us." 
 "Our next study needs to answer clear clinical questions: how well CYT-108 is tolerated across the planned doses and whether it shows preliminary signs of benefit for patients," said Tracy Goeken, MD, Chief Medical Officer of Cytonics. "FOCAL helps us evaluate candidate patient-selection criteria and the time needed to assess structural change. We plan to prioritize safety, tolerability and dose selection while exploring effects on pain and physical function. Structural assessments would generate hypotheses for longer-term studies; this early study is not intended to establish disease modification." 
 Why the approach is distinctive 
 Early-stage osteoarthritis trials are often designed around assumed rates of progression. FOCAL replaced those assumptions with modeled estimates from one of the largest long-term natural-history datasets in knee osteoarthritis. The analysis also built in validation steps that are uncommon at this stage of development: the phenotypes were derived and then reproduced in independent halves of the cohort, findings were confirmed across two imaging methods, and the patient-selection threshold was tested in held-out data. Over the course of the work, Cytonics also corrected its own earlier estimates. It moved to an adjudicated knee-replacement registry and a more conservative statistical model before finalizing any conclusions.
 Cytonics intends to extend FOCAL as new data become available, including data from its ongoing preclinical pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic program.
 About FOCAL 
 FOCAL (Foundational Osteoarthritis Clinical & Analytic Layer) is Cytonics' data-science program for osteoarthritis. It combines longitudinal natural-history data with CYT-108's biological mechanism to inform clinical development decisions. The analysis described here was led by Manjunath Kustagi, AI Engineer – Computational Biology, working with Cytonics' clinical development team, and Michelangelo Barone, MD, Head of Program Operations, who helped translate the FOCAL findings into recommendations for the planned CYT-108 trial. The findings are internal analyses of observational data. They have not been peer-reviewed or reviewed by any regulatory authority.
 Data and/or research tools used in the preparation of this release were obtained and analyzed from the controlled access datasets distributed from the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI), a data repository housed within the NIMH Data Archive (NDA). OAI is a collaborative informatics system created by the National Institute of Mental Health and the National Institute of Arthritis, Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) to provide a worldwide resource to quicken the pace of biomarker identification, scientific investigation and OA drug development. Dataset identifier(s): NIMH Data Archive Collection ID 2343. This release does not claim or imply endorsement by the NIH, NIMH or NIAMS of Cytonics, its research or CYT-108.
 About CYT-108 
 CYT-108 is an investigational recombinant variant of the endogenous alpha-2-macroglobulin (A2M) blood serum protein. The "bait" region of the protein, which serves as a substrate for proteases, was engineered to increase its affinity for specific proteases that are known to play a significant role in the molecular pathogenesis of osteoarthritis. The combination of both highly specific and broad-spectrum protease inhibition activity of CYT-108 differentiates this novel biologic from other attempts to develop small molecule inhibitors that target a single protease, positioning CYT-108 as an ideal disease-modifying candidate for osteoarthritis. The development of CYT-108 is predicated on the success of Cytonics' first-generation therapy, the Autologous Protease Inhibitor Concentrate (APIC) system, which is a 510(k) medical device that selectively enriches autologous A2M for intra-articular injection into joints containing articular cartilage (knee, shoulder, spine, hip, etc.). The clinical and commercial success of APIC uniquely de-risks the development of CYT-108 because it is already understood that high concentrations of A2M can be introduced into arthritic joints without significant side effects, and the treatment has achieved clinical and commercial success since it was first cleared by the FDA as a 510(k) device and sold in 2015.
 About Cytonics Corp. 
 Cytonics, founded in 2006, is a private research and development company focused on developing molecular diagnostics and therapeutics for chronic musculoskeletal diseases such as osteoarthritis. The company's flagship product was a diagnostic test (the Fibronectin-Aggrecan Complex Test, FACT) which helps identify the source of joint pain and assists physicians in determining the most appropriate course of treatment. Cytonics then developed the APIC system which concentrates a therapeutic blood protein, A2M, from patients' own blood and injects the A2M-rich concentrate into damaged joints. APIC has been used to treat over 8,000 patients nationwide, saving thousands of patients from invasive joint replacement surgeries. The company has raised over $25M in private funding and was awarded $1.8M in grants from the NIH to pursue their innovative research. The company is planning a Phase 1b/2a clinical study for their lead drug candidate, CYT-108, a recombinant variant of the endogenous alpha-2-macroglobulin protease inhibitor. If approved, CYT-108 may be the first and only disease-modifying therapy for osteoarthritis.

First-in-human evidence of exaluren-mediated readthrough of collagen IV in patients with nonsense mutation Alport syndrome
 Kidney biopsies showed increased collagen IV abundance and partially improved podocyte morphology in all three participants
 Exaluren was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events, nephrotoxicity or ototoxicity
 Published findings support the ongoing Phase 2b EXACT study 
 ARLINGTON, Mass. , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eloxx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: ELOX ), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing exaluren for the treatment of rare kidney diseases, today announced the publication of results from its Phase 2a proof-of-mechanism study of exaluren in nonsense mutation Alport syndrome in the Journal of Clinical Investigation (JCI). The open-access paper, "Phase 2a study of readthrough therapy in nonsense mutation Alport syndrome," is available at https://www.jci.org/articles/view/208623 .
 "To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration in humans that a genetically targeted readthrough therapy can restore production of a missing protein in kidney cells and improve cell structure in a genetic kidney disease," said Daniel P. Gale, MD, PhD, of the Department of Renal Medicine at University College London and lead author of the paper. "These findings provide a strong rationale for further clinical evaluation of this approach, including in the ongoing EXACT study."
 Study Design and Results 
 Study design. Three patients aged 12 to 18 years with autosomal recessive Alport syndrome and a COL4A4 premature termination codon received daily subcutaneous exaluren (0.75 mg/kg) for eight weeks in the open-label Phase 2a study (NCT05448755). The primary endpoint was safety and tolerability; secondary endpoints included pre- and post-treatment kidney biopsy assessments.
 Kidney biopsy findings. Post-treatment biopsies showed increased collagen α3(IV), α4(IV) and α5(IV) abundance, physiologically localized α5(IV), and partially improved podocyte morphology in all participants. Masked machine-learning analysis of electron microscopy images showed foot process width reductions of 46%, 14% and 16%. Exploratory analysis showed increased filtration slit density in all participants; mean density increased by 50%, reaching more than 80% of healthy control values.
 Clinical measures. Changes in proteinuria were inconsistent, and interpretation was limited by intra-patient variability and the short treatment duration. Hematuria persisted in all participants.
 Safety. Exaluren was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events, study discontinuations, nephrotoxicity or ototoxicity, including in adolescents with pre-existing kidney and hearing impairment. Most adverse events were Grade 1 and resolved spontaneously.
 About the Phase 2b EXACT Study 
 EXACT (NCT07523581) is a global, randomized, placebo-controlled, delayed-start trial of exaluren designed to enroll 24 patients with Alport syndrome caused by nonsense mutations in the COL4A3 , COL4A4 or COL4A5 genes. The primary efficacy endpoint of the initial 16-week placebo-controlled portion of the trial is the change in podocyte foot process effacement, measured as the change in filtration slit density on kidney biopsies, in non-U.S. pediatric patients and all adult patients. The first patients were dosed in September 2026. The Company expects to report topline data from the 16-week placebo-controlled portion in mid-2027 and 32-week data by the end of 2027.
 About Alport Syndrome 
 Alport syndrome is an inherited kidney disease caused by mutations in the COL4A5 (X-linked) or COL4A3 and COL4A4 (autosomal) genes, which encode the α3α4α5(IV) collagen network of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM). Nonsense mutations introduce premature stop codons that prevent production of full-length collagen IV and are associated with a poor prognosis, with kidney failure often occurring by early adulthood. There are currently no approved treatments for Alport syndrome.
 About Exaluren 
 Exaluren (formerly ELX-02) is an investigational, ribosome-targeting glycoside designed to accumulate in kidney cells and promote readthrough of premature stop codons, but not native stop codons, to enable production of full-length, functional proteins. Exaluren is being evaluated in the Phase 2b EXACT study in nonsense mutation Alport syndrome and in the planned Phase 2 EXPRESS study in nonsense mutation autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD).
 About Eloxx Pharmaceuticals 
 Eloxx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: ELOX ) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel, small-molecule product candidates designed to modulate the ribosome and promote readthrough of premature stop codons induced by nonsense mutations to enable the production of full-length proteins. Eloxx's lead product candidate, exaluren, is being developed for the treatment of rare kidney diseases, including nonsense mutation Alport syndrome and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). Eloxx has also exclusively licensed its product candidate, ZKN-013, to Almirall, S.A., which is developing it for the treatment of rare dermatological diseases associated with nonsense mutations.
